sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Close Grip Bodyweight Push Up is a variation of the standard push up that targets the triceps more intensely by placing the hands closer together.

By narrowing your hand placement to be in line with your chest and keeping your elbows tucked close to your body, you shift the load from the chest to the triceps.

This exercise is an excellent bodyweight movement for building triceps strength, arm size, and upper body pushing power without any equipment.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Greater triceps activation compared to standard push ups
- Builds functional upper body pressing strength
- No equipment required — can be done anywhere
- Strengthens the chest, shoulders, and core as secondary muscles
- Improves lockout strength beneficial for bench press performance
- Develops elbow joint stability and tendon strength
- Easily scalable by adjusting tempo, reps, or elevation

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Triceps

Secondary: Chest (Pectoralis Major), Anterior Deltoids, Core (Rectus Abdominis, Obliques), Serratus Anterior

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Get into a plank position with your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
2. Place your hands in line with your chest, close to your body — roughly shoulder-width apart or narrower.
3. Keep your fingers pointing forward and elbows close to your torso.
4. Engage your core and glutes to maintain a flat, rigid back.
5. Your feet can be together or slightly apart for balance.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Start with your hands in line with your chest, keeping them close into your body.
2. With a straight back, plank-like position, press yourself up until your arms are fully extended.
3. Lower your body back down until your chest touches the floor while keeping your elbows tucked in and maintaining a neutral spine.
4. Repeat for reps.
5. Focus on controlled movement throughout — avoid flaring your elbows outward.
6. Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you press up.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Flaring the elbows outward instead of keeping them tucked
- Letting the hips sag or pike upward, breaking the plank position
- Not lowering fully to the floor, reducing range of motion
- Hands placed too far forward (should be in line with chest, not face)
- Rushing through reps without controlling the eccentric (lowering) phase
- Holding your breath instead of breathing rhythmically
- Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- No equipment required
- A flat, stable surface (floor, mat, or ground)
- Optional: Exercise mat for wrist and hand comfort
- Optional: Resistance band around the back for added difficulty
- Optional: Elevated surface for feet to increase difficulty

sections.heading: Hand Placement
sections.content:
1. Place hands directly under or slightly inside your shoulders.
2. Hands should be in line with your chest, not your face or neck.
3. Keep fingers spread and pointing forward for a stable base.
4. Ensure both hands are evenly spaced — symmetry is key.
5. Avoid placing hands too close together (diamond position) unless intentionally progressing.
6. Wrists should be in a neutral, comfortable alignment.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Plank Position: Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
2. Core: Brace your abs as if preparing for a punch.
3. Glutes: Squeeze to keep hips level and prevent sagging.
4. Head: Keep in a neutral position, looking slightly ahead of your hands.
5. Feet: Together or hip-width apart for stability.
6. Elbows: Stay tight to the body throughout the movement.
7. Shoulders: Depressed and away from your ears.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Standard Push Up: Wider hand placement, more chest emphasis
- Diamond Push Up: Hands touching in a diamond shape, maximum triceps focus
- Incline Push Up: Hands elevated, easier variation for beginners
- Tricep Dips: Bodyweight movement targeting triceps from a different angle
- Decline Push Up: Feet elevated for increased difficulty and upper chest engagement
- Bench Press Close Grip: Barbell equivalent for heavier loading

sections.heading: Close Grip Push Up Variations
sections.content:
Close Grip Push Up: Standard close hand placement on floor
Elevated Close Grip Push Up: Feet on bench for added difficulty
Slow Tempo Close Grip Push Up: 3-4 second eccentric for time under tension
Banded Close Grip Push Up: Band around back for added resistance
Weighted Close Grip Push Up: Plate on back for progressive overload
Pause Rep Close Grip Push Up: Pause at the bottom for strength gains

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Wrist Pain: Use push up handles or fists to keep wrists neutral
Shoulder Discomfort: Reduce range of motion or try incline variation
Lack of Strength: Start with incline close grip push ups on a bench or wall
Elbow Pain: Widen hand placement slightly and reduce depth
Lower Back Issues: Focus on core bracing, consider knee push up variation
Learning Stage: Begin with standard push ups and gradually narrow grip over time
